title: Fleece Jackets in Nairobi: The Warm Layer Between Your Base and Your Rain Shell

excerpt: Which fleece jackets in Nairobi suit Kenyan trails? How 100, 200 and 300-weight fleece compare, fleece vs softshell and down, thrifted buying checks and care.

content:
Look for a full-zip, mid-weight (200-weight) polyester fleece when you shop for fleece jackets in Nairobi: it keeps you warm at Shipton's Camp on Mt Kenya, where clear nights can drop below −10°C, yet dries fast and stuffs into a daypack. Lighter 100-weight fleece suits day hikes near the city, while heavy 300-weight is mostly for camp.

Choosing between the fleece jackets in Nairobi is harder than it looks. Fleece comes in different weights, knits and cuts, and a thrifted rack mixes all of them. Below we explain which weight suits which Kenyan trail, how fleece compares with softshell and down, what to check on a pre-owned piece, how to wash it, and where to find fleece jackets in Nairobi without paying new-shop prices.

Quick Facts

  • Best all-round pick: among fleece jackets in Nairobi, a full-zip 200-weight (mid-weight) polyester fleece.
  • Fleece weights: 100 is light and breathable, 200 is the versatile middle, 300 is thick and warm but bulky.
  • Wind and rain: standard fleece is neither windproof nor waterproof, so it needs a rain shell over it.
  • Where it earns its place: the Aberdares (3,000-4,000 m), Mt Kenya's Point Lenana (4,985 m) and cold camp nights.
  • Wet performance: polyester fleece holds little water and dries far faster than cotton or wool.
  • Thrifted value: pre-owned fleece jackets in Nairobi wear slowly, so branded quality costs far less than new.
  • Care: wash at about 30°C, inside out, with no fabric softener, then air-dry.

What Makes a Good Hiking Fleece Jacket?

The best fleece jackets in Nairobi for hiking trap warm air close to your body, let sweat escape, dry quickly and move with you. Fabric weight, the zip, the fit and a few small details decide whether a fleece works on a mountain or only on a cold Nairobi evening.

Fleece is a brushed polyester knit. The brushing raises tiny fibres that hold still air, and still air is what keeps you warm. Polyester is hydrophobic, so the fibres themselves absorb very little water. That is why a damp fleece still feels warm and why it dries on a pack strap in an hour or two of sun, unlike a cotton hoodie that stays cold and heavy all day.

Which details matter on fleece jackets in Nairobi?

Look at four things before the logo. A full-length zip lets you vent on steep climbs and close up at a windy rest stop. A collar that zips up to the chin protects the neck when wind cuts across a ridge. Zipped hand pockets keep a phone or snack from falling out, and a chest pocket is handy if your backpack hip belt covers the hand pockets.

Elastic or bound cuffs stop cold air running up the sleeves, and a hem drawcord does the same at the waist. Thumb loops are a bonus on summit night, when gloves and sleeves keep sliding apart. A hood is optional; most hikers already carry a beanie or balaclava, and a hood can bunch under a rain shell's own hood.

How should a hiking fleece fit?

When you try fleece jackets in Nairobi, aim for a fit that is close but not tight. You want room for a thermal base layer underneath and enough space to pull a rain jacket over it without the shoulders binding. Raise both arms overhead: the hem should not ride above your belt and the cuffs should still cover your wrists. A fleece that is too loose lets warm air pump out every time you move.

Which Fleece Weight Do You Need: 100, 200 or 300?

Among fleece jackets in Nairobi, most Kenyan hikers are best served by a 200-weight fleece, with a 100-weight as a lighter second layer for warm-weather hikes. A 300-weight only makes sense for very cold, slow days such as camp evenings above 4,000 m.

The weight number describes how heavy the fabric is per square metre: higher numbers mean thicker, warmer and bulkier fabric. Labels on fleece jackets in Nairobi vary by brand, so treat the number as a guide. Feel the thickness, check how much it compresses, and hold it against the light; a thin microfleece shows light through it, a 300-weight does not.

Fleece typeFeel and warmthBest Kenyan use
100-weight / microfleeceThin, very breathable, packs smallNgong Hills, Karura, Mt Longonot starts; under a shell in the rain
200-weight (mid-weight)The versatile middle; layers well under a shellAberdares day hikes, Mt Kenya trekking days, most camping
300-weight (heavyweight)Thick and warm, bulky, less breathableCamp evenings and slow summit mornings above 4,000 m
Grid fleeceGrid inside for airflow; smooth face resists pillingFast hikes where you sweat on the climb and cool at the top
High-pile / sherpaVery warm for its weight, lets wind throughCamp wear and sleeping; less useful while walking
Wind-resistant (hard-face) fleeceSmooth, tighter outer face; cuts wind chillExposed ridges such as Lesatima or the Mt Kenya moorland

Is grid fleece worth paying extra for?

Grid fleece is worth it if you hike fast and sweat a lot. The grid of channels on the inside moves moisture out and dumps heat while you climb, then the lofted squares hold warmth when you stop. Its smoother outer face also pills less where a backpack rubs. For slow walkers and campers, a plain 200-weight does the same job for less money.

If you only buy one of the fleece jackets in Nairobi you are comparing, make it the mid-weight. You can make a 200-weight warmer by adding a thermal top underneath or a down jacket over it at camp, but you cannot make a 300-weight cooler on a sweaty forest climb, short of carrying it in your pack.

Where Will You Wear It? Fleece Jackets in Nairobi Matched to Kenyan Trails

Fleece jackets in Nairobi earn their keep on any hike that starts before sunrise or climbs above about 2,500 m. On lower trails a fleece is mostly worn at the start and summit; on the high mountains it can stay on all day.

Day hikes near Nairobi

Ngong Hills, Mt Longonot and Karura are warm by mid-morning, but the 6 a.m. matatu or car ride and the first windy ridge can feel cold, especially in the June-August cool season. That chilly first hour is the reason many day hikers own a fleece at all. Light 100-weight fleece jackets in Nairobi are enough here. You will probably take yours off within an hour, so pick one that rolls small. Our day-hike pillar, easy day hikes near Nairobi, lists which of these trails suit a first outing.

The Aberdares: Table Mountain, Elephant Hill and Oldoinyo Lesatima

The Aberdares are where fleece jackets in Nairobi face their hardest work, far more than on any trail near the city. The range is wet, misty and high: Oldoinyo Lesatima tops out at about 4,001 m and the Table Mountain hike climbs to roughly 3,800 m through bog and tussock grass. Wind across the moorland and drizzle can turn a sunny morning cold within minutes.

Wear a 200-weight fleece over a synthetic or merino base layer, with a rain shell in your pack. On the open moorland the shell goes on over the fleece, not instead of it. If you run cold, a wind-resistant fleece is the better choice for these exposed ridges.

Mt Kenya and Kilimanjaro

Mt Kenya is where mid-weight fleece jackets in Nairobi earn their price: a fleece is a daily layer from the moorland upwards. Nights at Shipton's or Mackinder's Camp are below freezing, and the pre-dawn push to Point Lenana (4,985 m) is the coldest part of the trek. Kenya Wildlife Service manages Mt Kenya National Park; check the official KWS website for current park information before you go.

For the summit push, most climbers wear a thermal base, a 200-weight fleece, a down or synthetic puffer and a waterproof shell. Our Mt Kenya gear shopping list covers the rest of the kit, and the same fleece-plus-puffer system works on Kilimanjaro.

Camping at Naivasha, Hell's Gate and the Rift Valley

Camping on the Rift Valley floor feels warm by day, but evenings beside Lake Naivasha can drop to around 10°C. A fleece is the layer you live in from sunset to breakfast. Here even the cosy high-pile or 300-weight fleece jackets in Nairobi stores sell are fine because you are not walking hard; pair one with a warm hat and a sleeping bag rated for the conditions.

Fleece, Softshell or Down: Which Mid-Layer Should You Buy?

Fleece jackets in Nairobi are the most forgiving mid-layer for Kenyan conditions because fleece breathes on the climb and stays warm when damp. Softshell blocks wind better, while down gives the most warmth for its weight but loses most of it when wet.

Is fleece better than softshell for hiking?

Fleece is warmer and more breathable than most softshells; softshell is more wind- and shower-resistant. Fleece lets wind straight through, so on a gusty ridge a plain fleece alone feels cold. A softshell has a tighter outer weave that stops much of the wind and sheds light drizzle, but it is usually less warm for its weight.

Many hikers combine them: a fleece for warmth, a rain shell or softshell over it for wind. Some jackets blend the two, with a fleece lining and a softshell face; we stock a fleece soft-shell jacket of this kind, which suits the Aberdares well.

Fleece or down jacket: which is warmer?

A down jacket is much warmer for its weight and packs smaller, but it should stay dry. Wet down clumps and stops insulating, which matters in the Aberdares and on Mt Kenya's wet forest sections. Fleece keeps working when damp and survives rough treatment such as scrambling and campfire smoke.

The practical answer for a Mt Kenya or Kilimanjaro climb is both: fleece while walking, down for camp and summit night. For day hikes near the city, one of the lighter fleece jackets in Nairobi is enough on its own. We explain the full system in our post on layering for cold-weather hikes.

How does fleece work with a rain jacket?

Treat fleece jackets in Nairobi as the middle of a three-layer system: base layer to move sweat, fleece to trap warmth, waterproof shell to block rain and wind. On its own a fleece soaks through in a downpour, so in the long rains (roughly March-May) and short rains (roughly October-December) always carry a shell. Our rain jacket range has shells that fit over a mid-weight fleece.

What Should You Check Before Buying a Second-Hand Fleece?

Second-hand fleece jackets in Nairobi are a good buy if the fabric still has loft, the zip runs smoothly and the cuffs still grip. Pilling alone is cosmetic; flattened, shiny patches and a broken zip are the real problems.

Fleece ages in predictable places. Backpack straps and hip belts rub the shoulders and sides, so check there first. Use this list when you compare fleece jackets in Nairobi, whether on our rails or anywhere else:

What to checkGood signWalk away if
Loft (thickness)Fabric springs back when you squeeze itFlat, matted or shiny patches at the shoulders
ZipRuns top to bottom without catchingMissing teeth, a slider that slips open
Cuffs and hemElastic still grips the wristStretched, wavy cuffs that let air in
PillingLight bobbles only (cosmetic)Bobbles so dense the fabric has thinned
Melt marksNoneHard, glossy spots from campfire sparks or an iron
LabelShows 100% polyester or a clear fibre blendCotton-heavy blends sold as hiking fleece
Fit over layersRoom for a base layer; shell fits over itTight at the shoulders or short at the wrists

How do fleece sizes run?

Sizes on fleece jackets in Nairobi vary between brands and between European, UK and US labels. Many US-brand fleeces are cut roomier, while some European and alpine brands fit slimmer. Ignore the letter on the label and try it on over the layer you will hike in. If you are ordering online, measure a fleece you already like across the chest, armpit to armpit, and send us that number on WhatsApp.

Pro Tips

  • Try fleece jackets on in Nairobi over a thermal top, not a T-shirt, so the fit matches the mountain.
  • For Mt Kenya, pick darker fleece jackets in Nairobi: they hide trail grime and dry faster in the sun.
  • A full zip beats a half-zip pullover on steep climbs because you can vent fully.
  • Pack the fleece at the top of your bag so it is ready at the first windy rest stop.
  • On summit night, wear the fleece under the puffer, never over it.
  • Carry a light 100-weight as a spare layer on long Aberdares days.

How Do You Wash and Care for a Fleece Jacket?

Thrifted or new, fleece jackets in Nairobi last longest when washed inside out on a gentle cycle at about 30°C, with no fabric softener, and left to air-dry. Most fleece damage comes from heat and softener, not from wear.

  1. Empty the pockets and close every zip so the teeth do not snag the fabric.
  2. Turn the fleece inside out to reduce friction and pilling on the outer face.
  3. Use a gentle or delicates cycle at around 30°C with a mild detergent; check the care label first.
  4. Skip fabric softener, because it coats the fibres and reduces breathability over time.
  5. Use a low spin, then hang the fleece on a line or rack in the shade; avoid tumble-drying and hot irons.
  6. Store it loosely folded, not compressed in a stuff sack, so the fibres keep their loft.

Fleece sheds tiny polyester fibres in the wash. Washing less often, using a full but not overloaded machine and catching fibres in a wash bag all help. After a dusty hike, a good shake and an airing are often enough instead of a full wash.

To remove pills, use a fabric shaver or a sharp razor drawn lightly across the surface. Do not pull them off by hand, which tugs more fibres loose. A well-cared-for thrifted fleece can easily last many more seasons of Kenyan hiking.

What Mistakes Do Hikers Make With Fleece?

The most common mistakes hikers make with fleece jackets in Nairobi are wearing one as the only outer layer in wind or rain, buying too heavy a weight, and hiking uphill in it until it is soaked with sweat.

Climbing in a fleece is the big one. On the forest climb out of a Mt Kenya gate or up Longonot's first slope, you will overheat quickly. Take the fleece off before you start sweating, then put it back on the moment you stop. Five minutes of discipline keeps it dry for the cold summit later.

Another mistake is choosing style over function. Some fleece jackets in Nairobi are fashion pieces: a thick high-pile jacket feels lovely in a café but lets the wind straight through on a ridge and takes up half a daypack. A plain technical 200-weight is lighter, warmer when it counts and cheaper second-hand.

Finally, many hikers forget that cotton underneath ruins the system. A cotton T-shirt under your fleece stays wet with sweat and chills you on every rest stop. Pair your fleece with a synthetic or merino base; our thermal wear guide explains the options, and the Kenya hiking gear checklist shows where a fleece fits in the full kit.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a fleece jacket warm enough for Mt Kenya?

A fleece jacket alone is not warm enough for Mt Kenya's summit night, when temperatures fall well below freezing. A 200-weight fleece is the right walking layer from the moorland upwards, but for Point Lenana you need it under a down or synthetic puffer and a windproof shell, with a thermal base layer next to the skin, a warm hat and insulated gloves.

Can I wear a fleece in the rain?

A fleece can handle light drizzle for a short time, but it is not waterproof and will soak through in steady rain. Polyester fleece still keeps some warmth when damp and dries quickly, which is why it beats cotton. In the long rains or short rains, wear a waterproof rain jacket over your fleece rather than relying on the fleece itself.

What's the difference between 100, 200 and 300 fleece?

The numbers describe fabric weight: 100 is thin and very breathable, 200 is a mid-weight that balances warmth and breathability, and 300 is thick and warm but bulky. Of all the fleece jackets in Nairobi, a 200-weight is the most useful single choice for the Aberdares and Mt Kenya trekking days. Use a 100 for warm day hikes.

Does fleece shrink in the wash?

Polyester fleece rarely shrinks in a normal 30°C wash, but high heat can damage it. Tumble-drying on hot, ironing or drying it against a heater can melt or flatten the fibres and leave it harsh and thin. Wash it inside out on a gentle cycle, skip the fabric softener and hang it in the shade to keep its loft.

Are second-hand fleece jackets in Nairobi worth buying?

Second-hand fleece jackets in Nairobi are often excellent value because polyester fleece wears slowly. A pre-owned branded fleece with good loft, a working zip and firm cuffs will keep you just as warm as a new one. Check the shoulders and sides for flattened patches where backpacks rub, and look for melt marks from campfires before you pay.

Final Thoughts

Warmth on a Kenyan mountain comes from layers working together, and the fleece sits right in the middle of that system. For most hikers the smart buy among fleece jackets in Nairobi is a full-zip 200-weight that fits over a base layer and under a rain shell, with a lighter 100-weight as a spare.
